Its exact conditional probability is binom(K+R-2n-1,R-2n-1)/binom(K+R-1,R-1), which tends to (1+beta)^(-2n)>0 when K/R tends to beta. claim_results.statement: For fixed admissible eta, lambda, bounded positive alphabet cutoff B_0, and a preregistered disjoint block grid with L_R=floor(c log R) below the stated symbolic-supply threshold, there is a constant C such that every sufficiently large actual accessible suffix array satisfies E[exp(-lambda * sum_{q in Q_R} 1_{C_q}) | S_R=K and the exact first-passage data] <= C/R. Here C_q is the event that block q has all pair totals in {1,...,B_0}, its entry state is not low, and it does not satisfy the exact positive amplified-resonance condition recorded in the inputs.
claim_results.domain: Uniformly over sufficiently large accessible suffix lengths R=2J+epsilon, epsilon in {0,1}, and the actual coupled integer arrays (r,R,tau,K) with K-beta R in (-15-2beta,-13-2beta), beta=log_2(3)-1, z_0=2^(1-{beta tau}) in (1,2), and S_R=K under the uniform weak-composition law; constants may depend only on the preregistered fixed parameters eta, lambda, B_0, c and the fixed grid rule, not on r,R,tau,K.
assumptions: Y_1,...,Y_R are nonnegative integers uniformly distributed over weak compositions with sum S_R=K; pair totals are B_j=Y_(2j-1)+Y_(2j).
At pair time j, H_j=B_1+...+B_j and z_j=2^(tau+floor(beta tau)+1+2j+H_j)/3^(tau+2j)=2^(1-{beta tau}+H_j-2beta j).
A low entry means z_j<eta. Low-state visits themselves are not rare and may not be discarded as an exceptional event.

For a bounded-positive L_R-word starting at j, positive amplified resonance is the exact event dist(2^(E_j)/3^(D_j+2L_R), Z)<eta/9^L_R with positive nearest integer, where E_j=tau+floor(beta tau)+1+2j+H_j and D_j=tau+2j.
C_q means bounded-positive useful block, non-low at entry, and nonresonant. The target permits many low or resonant blocks; it only requires sufficient weighted occupation of C_q blocks.
The desired estimate is an analytic uniform bound. Finite examples, numerical fits, agreement among models, or an unproved appeal to a named theorem do not prove it.

first_missing_step.name: Non-low bounded-positive block occupation inequality
first_missing_step.inequality: Let A_q be the event that every pair total in block q lies in {1,...,B_0} and the block entry satisfies z>=eta, with no resonance restriction. Prove that there exist C<infinity and R_0 such that, for every sufficiently large accessible R=2J+epsilon and every actual coupled array (r,R,tau,K) satisfying the frozen constraints, E[exp(-lambda * sum_{q in Q_R} 1_{A_q}) | S_R=K and the exact first-passage data] <= C/R.
first_missing_step.why_strictly_narrower: Since C_q is a subset of A_q, sum_q 1_{A_q} >= sum_q 1_{C_q}, so exp(-lambda sum 1_{A_q}) <= exp(-lambda sum 1_{C_q}). Therefore the primary claim implies this inequality. It removes the short-orbit resonance arithmetic and isolates the first unresolved occupation problem.
first_missing_step.why_not_proved_by_displayed_reductions: The beta-binomial formula controls one sampled height, and exact composition counts control one prescribed word. Neither controls the joint lower tail across a growing disjoint grid. Endpoint conditioning creates dependence, low visits have positive probability, and no proved cycle/ballot identity resolves the affine threshold, rational ties, even-time sampling, and odd singleton conventions. Moreover, proving this inequality alone would still not establish the primary claim because resonant deletion remains.
